summary: Ademetionine (S-adenosyl-L-methionine, SAMe) is a naturally occurring molecule that serves as the body's principal methyl-group donor and a precursor of glutathione. As a medicinal product (available in the EU, India and elsewhere; in the US it is sold only as a dietary supplement and is NOT FDA-approved as a drug - pending clinical review), it is used for intrahepatic cholestasis - including intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy - and as an adjunctive/alternative treatment for depressive symptoms. Typical doses are 800-1600 mg/day orally (enteric-coated tablets taken on an empty stomach) or 200-800 mg/day by IV/IM injection. It is generally well tolerated; the main cautions are precipitation of mania/hypomania in bipolar disorder, GI upset and anxiety/insomnia, and theoretical serotonergic interactions.

Adjunctive/alternative treatment of depressive symptoms / depressive syndromes

admin: Swallow enteric-coated tablets whole; do not chew or crush (the coating protects the active drug and the stomach)
Take tablets between meals (on an empty stomach), preferably in the morning given a mild stimulating effect
For parenteral use, reconstitute the lyophilised powder with the supplied solvent immediately before administration; give IM, or IV slowly/by infusion
Do not mix parenteral ademetionine with alkaline or calcium-containing solutions
Use freshly prepared parenteral solution; discard if discoloured
moa: Ademetionine (SAMe) is synthesised endogenously from methionine and ATP and is the principal methyl-group donor in the body. It participates in three key metabolic pathways: transmethylation (donating methyl groups for synthesis of phospholipids, proteins, nucleic acids, and neurotransmitters - improving hepatocyte membrane fluidity and bile-salt transport, which relieves cholestasis); transsulphuration (a precursor for cysteine, glutathione, and taurine, supporting hepatic antioxidant defence and detoxification); and aminopropylation (polyamine synthesis for cell regeneration). In depression, increased methylation supports synthesis of monoamine neurotransmitters (dopamine, noradrenaline, serotonin), proposed to underlie its antidepressant effect.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to ademetionine or excipients
Genetic defects affecting the methionine cycle / causing homocystinuria or hyperhomocysteinaemia (e.g. cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency, vitamin B12 metabolism defects)
relative: Bipolar affective disorder (risk of switch to mania/hypomania)
Pregnancy in the first trimester (use only if essential)
Patients with low vitamin B12/folate (monitor homocysteine)
monitor: Liver biochemistry / cholestasis markers (bilirubin, ALP, GGT, bile acids)
Mood, and emergence of mania/hypomania in predisposed patients
Signs of serotonergic excess if combined with antidepressants

preg: Ademetionine is an endogenous substance and has been used, including in clinical studies, for intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy in the second and third trimesters, where benefit on pruritus and cholestasis has been reported. Data in the first trimester are limited; use during the first trimester only if clearly necessary. Follow the regional SmPC and specialist advice.
lact: There are limited data on the excretion of ademetionine in human milk. As it is an endogenous compound, modest risk is expected, but it should be used during breastfeeding only if clearly needed and under medical supervision.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is established for renal impairment; ademetionine is largely incorporated into endogenous metabolic pathways. Use with caution and monitor in significant renal impairment.
hepatic: Ademetionine is used therapeutically in liver disease and intrahepatic cholestasis; hepatic impairment is generally a treatment indication rather than a contraindication. Monitor liver biochemistry and clinical response; severe hepatic encephalopathy warrants caution.

major: Serotonergic drugs - SSRIs, SNRIs, MAOIs, tricyclics, tramadol, triptans, St John's Wort (theoretical additive serotonergic effect / serotonin syndrome)
moderate: Levodopa (SAMe may increase methylation of levodopa, theoretically reducing its effect)
Other antidepressants (additive mood effects; mania risk in bipolar disorder)
minor: Drugs affecting the folate/B12 / homocysteine pathway

interactions.alcohol: Avoid - alcohol aggravates the underlying liver disease being treated
interactions.diagnostics: May lower plasma homocysteine; ensure adequate folate and vitamin B12 status

counsel: Swallow tablets whole on an empty stomach, ideally in the morning (it can be mildly stimulating)
It may take a few weeks to feel the full effect on mood
Tell your doctor if you have bipolar disorder - this medicine can trigger a high/manic mood
Report agitation, racing heartbeat, sweating, or confusion if you also take antidepressants (serotonin syndrome)
Avoid alcohol, which harms the liver
Tell your clinician about all antidepressants, levodopa, and supplements you take
Ensure adequate vitamin B12 and folate intake as advised
pk: Cholestasis/mood benefit develops over days to weeks of treatment
Oral (enteric-coated) plasma peak ~3-5 hours; bioavailability is low and increased when taken between meals
Short plasma half-life - given in divided daily doses
Store tablets below 25 degrees C protected from moisture; reconstitute parenteral form immediately before use and protect from light
pearls: NOT FDA-approved as a medicine - in the US, SAMe is sold only as a dietary supplement; this record is based on EU/Indian SmPC sources and is pending clinical review.

SAMe is the body's main methyl donor and a glutathione precursor - it relieves cholestasis (improves bile-salt transport and membrane fluidity) and supports monoamine synthesis (antidepressant effect).
Take enteric-coated tablets on an empty stomach in the morning - food lowers absorption and a late dose can cause insomnia.
Can precipitate mania/hypomania in bipolar disorder; theoretical serotonin syndrome with serotonergic antidepressants.
Used for intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (2nd/3rd trimester) in clinical practice; follow specialist guidance.
Contraindicated in inborn errors of the methionine cycle (homocystinuria); ensure adequate B12/folate to avoid raising homocysteine.
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember earlier in the day. If it is late in the day or almost time for the next dose, skip it (taking it late may cause insomnia) and resume your normal schedule. Do not take a double dose.
overdose: Ademetionine has a wide safety margin as an endogenous compound and no specific antidote exists. Overdose is most likely to cause exaggerated GI effects (nausea, diarrhoea), anxiety, insomnia, or, in predisposed individuals, agitation/mania. Management is supportive and symptomatic, with observation and reassurance; discontinue the drug and treat severe agitation or any serotonergic features supportively.
